docs.title: densnv
docs.text:
Exploratory analysis of the SINAVE vector-borne disease datasets of Mexico, in Python. It is the Python version of the R package densnv, part of the dengueverse.

In development

Ready: reading and aggregating the cases (module 1), the effective reproductive number, Rt (module 2), and the active transmission foci with the diagnosis of the epidemiological scenario (module 3), and the main graphs and maps (module 4).

import densnv

loc = densnv.cases_by_loc("DENGUE2_.txt", "DENV")
loc.explore(column="probable")

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
1. Read: read(), read_sinave(), read_dengue_dataset().
  2. Aggregate: cases_by_agem() (municipalities), cases_by_loc() (localities), cases_week() (weeks).
  3. Rt: rt_dengue() for the country, a state, a municipality or a locality (Cori et al. 2013, the same estimates as EpiEstim).
  4. Active foci: mp_active_foci(): DBSCAN / ST-DBSCAN, Knox test, transmission and control zones, blocks to treat and diagnosis of the epidemiological scenario (focalised, dispersed, generalised, early warning) with the operational strategy.
  5. Graphs and maps: plt_heatmap(), plt_pyramid(), plt_serotype(), plt_treemap(), mp_bumpmap(), mp_cases_loc() and mp_serotype().

The results are the same as in R: every function is validated against densnv with the real SINAVE dataset.

docs.title: Data
docs.text: The SINAVE datasets are for the exclusive use of the staff of the State Ministries of Health and of the federal level. The package reads them from your computer; it never downloads or publishes them.

docs.title: 0.1.0 (in development)
docs.text:
1. Module 1: read(), read_sinave(), read_dengue_dataset(), cases_by_agem(), cases_by_loc() and cases_week().
  2. Module 2: rt_dengue(), with estimate_r() and discr_si() (the parametric serial interval method of EpiEstim).
  3. Module 3: mp_active_foci() (DBSCAN / ST-DBSCAN, Knox test, zones, blocks and diagnosis of the epidemiological scenario), with an interactive map (folium, optional).
  4. Module 4: graphs (plt_heatmap(), plt_pyramid(), plt_serotype(), plt_treemap()) and maps (mp_bumpmap(), mp_cases_loc(), mp_serotype()); each returns the table behind the figure.

docs.title: Español
docs.text:
densnv es la versión en Python del paquete de R densnv para el análisis exploratorio de las bases de datos de Enfermedades Transmitidas por Vector del SINAVE. Es parte del dengueverse.

En desarrollo

Listos: la lectura y agregación de casos (módulo 1), el número reproductivo efectivo, Rt (módulo 2), y los focos activos de transmisión con el diagnóstico del escenario epidemiológico (módulo 3), y las principales gráficas y mapas (módulo 4).

docs.title: Ejemplo
docs.text:
import densnv

x   = densnv.read("~/sinave/2026", vbd="DENGUE")
mpo = densnv.cases_by_agem("~/sinave/2026", "DENGUE", status_case=[1, 2])
loc = densnv.cases_by_loc("~/sinave/2026/DENGUE2_.txt", "DENV")
r   = densnv.cases_week("~/sinave/2026", mpo="MERIDA", year=2026)

# Rt de la localidad de Mérida, ventana de 4 semanas
dataset = densnv.read_sinave("~/sinave/2026/DENGUE2_.txt")
rt = densnv.rt_dengue(dataset, level="locality", cve_edo="31",
                      cve_mpo="050", cve_loc="0001", window_days=28)
rt["rt_ventana"]

# focos activos y escenario epidemiológico (casos geocodificados z)
res = densnv.mp_active_foci(z, cve_edo="31", locality="Merida",
                            temporal_scale=28, buffer_m=0, method="st-dbscan",
                            n_sim=999, seed=123, print_map=True)
res["diagnostico"]["tabla"]

Las claves geográficas son texto con ceros a la izquierda ("31", "050", "0001") y los nombres conservan sus acentos.

docs.title: Datos
docs.text: Las bases del SINAVE son para uso exclusivo del personal de las Secretarías de Salud estatales y del nivel federal. El paquete las lee de tu computadora; nunca las descarga ni las publica.

docs.title: Read the SINAVE files
docs.text:
read() reads every txt file of a folder whose name contains vbd:

import densnv

x = densnv.read("~/sinave/2026", vbd="DENGUE")            # all the columns
x = densnv.read("~/sinave/2026", vbd="DENGUE", complete=False)  # arbovirus columns

The geographic keys are zero-padded text (CVE_EDO_REP == "31", CVE_MPO_REP == "050", CVE_LOC_REP == "0001"), the status, year and week are integers and the dates are datetimes. The names keep their accents ("YUCATÁN").

docs.title: Cases by municipality and locality
docs.text:
mpo = densnv.cases_by_agem("~/sinave/2026", "DENGUE", status_case=[1, 2],
                           country=False, cve_edo="31")
mpo.plot(column="n", legend=True)

loc = densnv.cases_by_loc("~/sinave/2026/DENGUE2_.txt", "DENV", week=range(1, 11))
loc.sort_values("probable", ascending=False).head()

docs.title: Cases by week
docs.text:
r = densnv.cases_week("~/sinave/2026", mpo="MERIDA", year=2026)
r["estatus"]        # probable, confirmed and estimated by week
r["figure"]         # matplotlib figure

docs.title: Effective reproductive number (Rt)
docs.text:
dataset = densnv.read_sinave("~/sinave/2026/DENGUE2_.txt")

rt = densnv.rt_dengue(dataset, level="locality", place="REP",
                      cve_edo="31", cve_mpo="050", cve_loc="0001",
                      window_days=28)
rt["rt_ventana"]    # Rt of the last 28 days, 95% CrI and phase
rt["rt"]            # Rt curve (weekly sliding windows)
rt["figure"]        # matplotlib figure

docs.title: Active transmission foci and epidemiological scenario
docs.text:
# geocoded cases: columns long, lat, ESTATUS_CASO, FEC_INI_SIGNOS_SINT, CVE_*_REP
res = densnv.mp_active_foci(z, cve_edo="31", locality="Merida",
                            temporal_scale=28, buffer_m=0,
                            method="st-dbscan", n_sim=999, seed=123,
                            print_map=True)
res["foci"]                      # active foci, Knox test by focus
res["blocks"]                    # blocks to treat
res["diagnostico"]["tabla"]      # scenario, criteria and action
res["map"]                       # interactive map (pip install folium)

docs.title: Graphs and maps
docs.text:
Each function returns the table behind the figure (data) and the figure.

pip install "densnv[plots] @ git+https://github.com/fdzul/densnv-py"   # plotly, squarify, folium

ds = densnv.read_sinave("~/sinave/2026/DENGUE2_.txt")

densnv.plt_heatmap(ds, state="YUCATAN", year=2026, status=[1, 2])["figure"]   # plotly
densnv.plt_pyramid(ds, title="Casos confirmados")["figure"]                   # matplotlib
densnv.plt_serotype(ds, year=2026)["figure"]
densnv.plt_treemap(ds, country=True, year=2026)["figure"]
densnv.mp_bumpmap(ds, year=2026)["figure"]

loc = densnv.cases_by_loc("~/sinave/2026/DENGUE2_.txt", "DENV")
densnv.mp_cases_loc(loc, var="probable", top_n=10)["map"]                    # folium
densnv.mp_serotype("~/sinave/2026/DENGUE2_.txt", cve_edo="31")["map"]

Name Type Description Default path str or Path

Folder with the SINAVE txt files (the dengue file has "DEN" in its name).

Municipality(ies) of report in uppercase, as in SINAVE (DES_MPO_REP).

Year (ANO).

Also draw the figure (matplotlib).

True

"manejo": probable + confirmed cases by week and management (hospitalised / outpatient); "estatus": probable, confirmed and estimated cases by week (estimated = positivity × probable + confirmed); "figure": the matplotlib figure (None when plot=False).

Effective reproductive number (Rt) of dengue.

Rt for the country, a state, a municipality or a locality, from the daily incidence of the SINAVE cases and a parametric serial interval (Cori et al. 2013), as rt_dengue() of densnv in R.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default dataset DataFrame

SINAVE dengue dataset (e.g. densnv.read_sinave("DENGUE2_.txt")). It needs FEC_INI_SIGNOS_SINT, ESTATUS_CASO and, depending on level and place, CVE_EDO_*, CVE_MPO_* and CVE_LOC_*.

required level ('country', 'state', 'municipality', 'locality') "country" place ('REP', 'RES')

Place used to select the cases: of report (default; the cases are geocoded with it) or of residence. In non-endemic areas the cases are reported where they were exposed, so the place of report is the place of transmission.

"REP" cve_edo (str, int or list)

INEGI keys of the state, municipality and locality. cve_mpo and cve_loc can be lists of the same length (pairs).

None cve_mpo (str, int or list)

INEGI keys of the state, municipality and locality. cve_mpo and cve_loc can be lists of the same length (pairs).

None cve_loc (str, int or list)

INEGI keys of the state, municipality and locality. cve_mpo and cve_loc can be lists of the same length (pairs).

None status_caso int or list of int

1 probable, 2 confirmed.

(1, 2) ref_date str or date

Reference date; by default the latest date of onset of the cases.

None period_days int

Days, up to ref_date, of the daily incidence (default 365).

365 window_days int

Days, up to ref_date, of the window whose Rt gives the phase of the outbreak (default 21).

21 mean_si float

Mean and standard deviation (days) of the serial interval (21, 6.1).

21 std_si float

Mean and standard deviation (days) of the serial interval (21, 6.1).

21 plot bool

Draw the Rt curve (matplotlib).

True

Returns:

Type Description dict

rt (Rt of the weekly sliding windows with at least 10 cases, or None), rt_ventana (Rt of the window, its 95% credible interval and the phase: "En ascenso", "Estable", "En descenso" or "Sin estimar"), incidencia (daily incidence), area (name of the area) and figure (or None).

Notes

The curve uses weekly sliding windows with at least 10 cases that start at least mean_si + 2 * std_si days after the first date of onset of the dataset or of the period, whichever is later; before it the infectiousness of the previous cases is unknown and Rt is overestimated. The last days are usually incomplete (delay of report), which lowers Rt at the end.

Rt with a parametric serial interval (EpiEstim::estimate_R(), method "parametric_si").

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default incidence array - like

Daily incidence (cases per day, consecutive days). As in EpiEstim, the cases of the first day are taken as imported.

required t_start array-like of int

Start and end (1-based, inclusive) of each time window.

required t_end array-like of int

Start and end (1-based, inclusive) of each time window.

required mean_si float

Mean and standard deviation (days) of the serial interval.

21 std_si float

Mean and standard deviation (days) of the serial interval.

21 mean_prior float

Mean and standard deviation of the gamma prior of Rt.

5 std_prior float

Mean and standard deviation of the gamma prior of Rt.

5

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

One row per window: t_start, t_end, mean, std and the quantiles q025 ... q975 of the posterior of Rt.

Discretised serial interval: gamma distribution shifted by one day.

Same as EpiEstim::discr_si().

Active dengue transmission foci and diagnosis of the epidemiological scenario.

Python version of mp_active_foci() of densnv (R). It identifies the active transmission foci of a locality with DBSCAN (window) or ST-DBSCAN, delimits the transmission and control zones, selects the blocks to treat, tests the space-time interaction with the Knox test (global and by focus), estimates Rt with :func:rt_dengue and diagnoses the epidemiological scenario with the operational strategy.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default geocoded_dataset DataFrame

Geocoded cases with long, lat (EPSG:4326), ESTATUS_CASO and FEC_INI_SIGNOS_SINT; for Rt also the CVE_*_REP (or RES) keys.

required cve_edo str or int

INEGI state key of the locality.

required locality str

Name of the locality (as in rgeomex.extract_locality()).

required status_caso int or list of int

1 probable, 2 confirmed.

(1, 2) spatial_scale float

Spatial window in metres (flight range of Aedes aegypti, 400).

400 temporal_scale int

Temporal window in days (intrinsic + extrinsic incubation, 21).

21 min_cases int

Minimum cases in the space-time window to define a focus (3).

3 buffer_m float

Buffer of the control zone around the transmission zone (200 m).

200 ref_date str or date

Reference date; by default the latest onset in the locality.

None method ('window', 'st-dbscan')

Fixed window or space-time DBSCAN (new and persistent foci).

"window" n_sim int

Permutations of the Knox test (0 skips it).

999 perm_days int

Days, up to ref_date, of the cases used by the Knox test and by ST-DBSCAN (>= temporal_scale).

365 alpha float

Significance level (Holm-adjusted p-value by focus; Poisson test).

0.05 seed int

Seed of the permutations.

None place ('REP', 'RES')

Place of the cases used for Rt.

"REP" mean_si float

Serial interval for Rt (21, 6.1 days).

21 std_si float

Serial interval for Rt (21, 6.1 days).

21 capacity_cases float

Operational capacity: cases per week the brigades can work.

None coverage_min float

Coverage of the locality by the recent cases to consider them dispersed; by default 0.40 with 21 days, 0.50 with 28 and linear in between.

None foci_min float

Proportion of the recent cases in foci from which the cases are also considered dispersed (0.9).

0.9 print_map bool

Return the interactive map (folium) in map.

False save bool

Save the selected blocks as a GeoPackage in dir.

False dir str

Folder where the blocks are saved.

'./'

Returns:

Type Description dict

foci, transmission, blocks, cases (GeoDataFrames in EPSG:4326, None without foci), knox (global Knox test), diagnostico (tabla, escenario, accion, detalle, rt, rt_figure, casos_ventana, casos_mes, pct_pares_tiempo, cobertura_casos, pct_casos_en_focos, pct_area_transmision) and map (folium, or None).
